marie_support: FYI escalation from JB (customer_jb). Streaming SSE connections keep disconnecting after ~2m. Client reports 401 mid-stream, partial output (no final tokens / missing end-of-stream marker). Customer attached pcap + host-side trace: https://s3.redwood-dev/prod-captures/jb/streaming-1814999990.pcap ; trace_id=0x7f4b2d

deploy-bot: New support escalation created: ESCL-4817 assigned to @marie_support :rotating_light:

raj_engineer: looking. quick q: are they rotating bearer tokens while a stream is open? that often causes mid-connection 401s if the server validates per-chunk

customer_jb: yes, we refresh client access tokens about every 90s (corporate policy). we attempted to silently refresh and replay with a reconnect but sometimes the server returns duplicate chunks or missing end signals. we've captured the tcpdump above.

alex_sre: I pulled the pcap. I can already see TLS session rehandshakes then a FIN after a 401 response from the edge. posting a couple of log snippets we see on our side:

```
[2026-03-10T14:23:51.987Z] request_id=0x7f4b2d path=/v1/stream event=stream_write size=1024 status=200
[2026-03-10T14:25:32.124Z] request_id=0x7f4b2d path=/v1/stream event=auth_check status=401 err=token_expired
[2026-03-10T14:25:32.125Z] request_id=0x7f4b2d path=/v1/stream event=stream_close reason=auth_failure
```

ciara_prodops: metrics show a small spike in 401s from the customer's egress IP at 14:25UTC, matching their timeline. Also see increased connection reset counts on the edge around the same time.

raj_engineer: this matches a known behavior: our runtime currently validates auth on long-lived requests at each chunk boundary; a 401 triggers stream termination rather than signaling the client to resume. two mitigation routes:
- short-term: increase token TTL for this customer or provide a refresh token via a side-channel so they don't rotate mid-stream.
- mid-term: add resume semantics on the server to accept a rotated token if client reopens within an acceptable window and includes a resume cursor/event-id.

marie_support: customer asked for a concrete repro they can run locally to surface the problem. can we provide a minimal repro + suggested client-side workaround?

raj_engineer: yes. minimal repro steps (Linux):
1) start an EventSource-like stream using curl with a short-lived token:

```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gptx&stream=true"
```

2) after ~60-90s rotate $TOKEN to a new value (simulate your refresh).
3) observe server 401 and connection close in tcpdump.

example node client with reconnect+resume hints (pseudo):

```
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
let lastEventId = null;
es.addEventListener('message', e => { lastEventId = e.lastEventId; /* append chunk */ });
es.onerror = async () => {
  // refresh token via standard flow
  token = await refresh();
  // re-open with ?cursor=lastEventId or X-Last-Event-Id header
  es.close();
  es = new EventSource(url + `?cursor=${lastEventId}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
};
```

alex_sre: note: we currently only support cursor-based resumes for certain endpoints. for streaming text generation we emit a resume token in the stream header as `X-Resume-Token` early in the session (customers that use it can reconnect and ask to continue). if not used, the stream is considered ephemeral and on auth failure we close. we should ensure this behavior is documented.

customer_jb: they say they never saw an X-Resume-Token in the initial response headers. marie, can you confirm?

marie_support: checked original request logs: initial response headers for request_id=0x7f4b2d did not include X-Resume-Token. looks like the resume token feature wasn't enabled on their tenant (flag off).

ciara_prodops: quick config check: tenant jb-42 has resume_tokens=false in the runtime feature flags. i'm going to flip it to true in staging and can roll to prod on approval.

raj_engineer: if we enable resume tokens for jb-42 we get two benefits: 1) client can re-auth+reconnect with ?cursor / X-Last-Event-Id and continue, 2) we'll emit clearer metrics when clients reconnect after auth failures. caveat: resume window is 5m by default, so client must reconnect quickly.

marie_support: suggested immediate customer workaround: temporarily extend token TTL or run token refresh less frequently than the 2m stream length (e.g., rotate every 10m) OR enable the resume_tokens feature. Customer agreed to try increasing TTL for testing.

alex_sre: operational steps I will take now:
- bump TCP keepalive at edge (nginx/gateway) from 60s -> 120s for this tenant to reduce TLS rehandshakes.
- enable resume_tokens flag on a canary host for jb-42.
- add a short-lived metric: resume_attempts_by_tenant + failed_resumes to help quantify.

raj_engineer: follow-up engineering plan:
- patch runtime to accept Authorization header rotation for in-flight streams when the client provides X-Resume-Token and matches cursor (safety checks). low-risk canary: 2 hosts next week.
- add docs + client example for best practices (heartbeats every 15s, handle 401 by refreshing token and reconnecting with cursor).

marie_support: I've put the customer on a test window to try extended TTL and will report back in a few hours. also creating internal task ENG-9235 to add a small KB article and triage notes.

customer_jb: testing now. will update. thanks for the quick triage. :+1:

ciara_prodops: update: enabled resume_tokens on one canary host and bumped keepalive. logs show a successful reconnect from their IP where client reconnected with X-Last-Event-Id and we resumed output (no duplicate tokens, final [DONE] emitted). sample successful log:

```
[2026-03-10T15:02:11.201Z] request_id=0x7f4b2d path=/v1/stream event=resume request_id_prev=0x7f4b2d resume_cursor=e-8342 status=200
[2026-03-10T15:02:11.202Z] request_id=0x7f4b2d path=/v1/stream event=stream_write size=512 status=200
[2026-03-10T15:02:12.700Z] request_id=0x7f4b2d path=/v1/stream event=stream_end reason=complete
```

marie_support: great. next steps:
- short-term: keep canary on and ask customer to validate for 24h.
- mid-term: schedule ENG rollout for resume token acceptance + docs.
- support: send customer KB with repro steps + node/curl examples and suggested token TTL guidance.

raj_engineer: one more note — instrumented an internal metric to count partial-stream closures with code=auth_failure; will alert if rate increases post-rollout.

customer_jb: confirmed resume behavior looks good in their staging run. final tokens returned and no duplicate text. thanks everyone. :tada:

marie_support: closing the escalation after 24h verification. will reopen if customer sees recurrence. :eyes:
